verdict.rationale: Codegen has org-level agent-permission toggles: one controls whether the agent may create pull requests, others enforce signed commits and govern auto-applying repository rules. Agent-behavior settings can make agents present a structured plan, or respond only to explicit mentions, and runs can be paused and resumed via the API. Together these give some control over what the agent does unattended, but they are individual switches rather than tiered autonomy levels. Missing for 10: a defined tiered autonomy model (e.g. suggest / approve / auto levels), explicit plan-approval gating before execution, per-action confirmation policies, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.
